comment: The representative NuGet libraries' own test suites on WitOS (plan step N2.2, RFC 0015 section 9's gate N2), which @Docs/Implementation/N2.2-Library-Suites.md explains. repositories: each library's repository at the commit its pinned package (N2.1) was built from, with the submodules a suite needs and the SDK its global.json asks for when the host's does not serve it (sdks pins each by the SHA-256 of its linux-x64 archive). suites: test projects built unchanged for one framework of theirs, each in a group that runs as one boot (CI runs each group as a job of its own) and run on the host, then in the guest, by the runner their repository uses: xunit2 is xunit's console runner (xunitConsole), xunit3 the test project's own in-process runner, nunitlite NUnitLite, through program when the project is no program itself. excluded: 'class:' or 'method:' and a full name, left out of both runs, each with its reason. Every other test runs in both and must pass in the guest as on the host.

excluded.class:MemoryPack.Tests.GeneratorDiagnost: fails on Linux too, on .NET 8 and 10 alike: the tests compile against the assemblies loaded when the module initializer ran, where xunit's console runner had not loaded System.Private.Uri, so the generator stops with 'Type System.Uri is not found in compilation' (CS8785); upstream runs them under VSTest, whose adapter at this commit (xunit.runner.visualstudio 2.4.5) the SDK's test platform no longer loads
excluded.method:MemoryPack.Tests.Fuzz.Random: fails on the Linux host now and then (CI 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22, three runs): it serializes objects of random content, and FluentAssertions 6's equivalency throws NullReferenceException in StringEqualityEquivalencyStep.ValidateSubjectIsString when a random dictionary holds a null string, a flake of the test's own independent of WitOS, where a host failure fails the suite
excluded.method:MemoryPack.Tests.WellknownFormatt: writes past the end of a BitArray's array on .NET 10 (P5, @Docs/Implementation/P5-MemoryPack-Crash.md): MemoryPack 1.21.4's BitArrayFormatter reinterprets a BitArray through Unsafe.As as { int[] m_array; int m_length; int _version }, the layout up to .NET 9, while .NET 10's BitArray holds { byte[] _array; int _bitLength; int _version }, so the round trip of 1000 bits reads 375 bytes past the source's byte[125] and copies 125 * 4 bytes into the new one, over the memory the allocator hands out next; the suite died now and then on the Linux host as in the guest (with the test 7 of 100 runs on Linux under heap verification, without it none of 100), and the issue Cysharp/MemoryPack#460 names the technique

excluded.class:NUnit.Framework.Tests.SolutionTest: reads the repository's nuspec and project files, which the guest's volume does not hold: it holds the suite's build output
reads the repository's nuspec and project files, which the guest's volume does not hold: it holds the suite's build output
asserts that comparing large collections takes at most 250 ms, which the emulated processor exceeds (3.8 s)
runs on every platform but Linux and expects Windows' directory separator there, the inference 'not Linux, so Windows' that fails on WitOS (Compatibility-Differences: Platform identity)
excluded.class:NUnit.Framework.Tests.Attributes.C: gives its sample tests 50 ms before cancellation against delays of 500 ms, and the emulated processor can spend either compiling the path before the timer or the delay starts, so a test expected to be cancelled runs to completion or one expected to finish is cancelled (on ARM64 in CI: CancelAfterCausesOtherwisePassingTestToFailWithoutDebuggerAttached)
excluded.method:NUnit.Framework.Tests.TestContext: counts the assembly's default properties, and NUnit sets _PID from Process.GetCurrentProcess(), which throws PlatformNotSupportedException on WitOS (Compatibility-Differences: Processes)
excluded.method:NUnit.Framework.Tests.Constraints: counts how often a delegate is polled every 100 ms for 1.5 s and expects 5 to 16 calls, where a poll on the emulated processor can outlast its interval (NUnit's own comment on the test calls it flaky)
excluded.method:NUnit.Framework.Tests.Api.TestAss: gives a new runner 2 s to start the first of its slow tests, which the emulated processor can spend compiling the runner's path
is declared for Linux by SupportedOSPlatform or UnsupportedOSPlatform, and WitOS is not Linux (Compatibility-Differences: Platform identity), so the guest runs the opposite set of these tests from the host's

excluded.method:NUnit.Framework.Tests.AsyncVoidTe: runs a test whose async void method throws after a delay of 10 ms and whose teardown sleeps a second so that the exception reaches NUnit, which the emulated processor on four processors can spend compiling the continuation's path and dispatching the exception, so the result is not the error expected (CI's ARM64 leg, 2026-10-21; x64, 2026-10-23): a probe in the guest on four processors measured the first throw at 445 ms (x64) and 411 ms (ARM64) of the guest's time against 15 ms on the Linux host, and a continuation delayed up to 1.5 s while the thread pool's threads slept, on the host as in the guest
gives itself MaxTime(1000) for an assertion that fails and is caught, which the emulated processor on four processors can spend compiling that path and dispatching the exception the first time, so MaxTime fails the test (CI's ARM64 leg, 2026-10-21)

excluded.method:XunitTestAssemblyRunnerTests+Mess: expects xunit's description of its parallelism to say 'N threads', which xunit writes '1 thread' on a machine of one processor, as WitOS is until phase P (Compatibility-Differences: Processors); on Linux under taskset -c 0 it fails too
excluded.method:CoreTestAssemblyRunnerTests+Run.P: expects the second of two tests to start while the first sleeps 50 ms, which the emulated processor can spend compiling the second's path, so the first wakes before the second starts (on ARM64 in CI)
excluded.method:XunitTestRunnerTests+Timeout.With: gives the test 10 ms, which the emulated processor spends before it enters the test, compiling its path, so the test never takes the token the timeout cancels
